items.speaker: Evelyn
items.text: Hello, Ana. This is reception. Someone can come to your room at seven this evening, not six. We have two towels for you here. You can collect them now, or we can bring them at seven. Please tell us what you need. Thank you!

items.speaker: Ruby
items.text: Hi, Ana! Thank you for looking for my gift. I like the green T-shirt. Medium is right for me. I don’t need a jacket. Twelve dollars is OK. Can you bring the T-shirt on Friday? We can meet at the café. Thank you!

items.speaker: Niamh
items.text: Hi, Ana! You asked about my Sunday. I didn’t visit the museum in the end. The weather was beautiful, so I went to the beach instead.

items.speaker: Niamh
items.text: I walked for an hour and took some photos. Then I had lunch with a friend. It was a quiet afternoon, but I really enjoyed it. What did you do?

items.speaker: Owen
items.text: Hi, Ana! A quick update about the move: the lift isn’t working this afternoon. We have to take the stairs. The heavy box can stay downstairs for now, but I need help carrying the small bags. Could you come at three? I’m still going to paint tomorrow, so there’s no need to bring paint today. Thank you!

items.speaker: Evelyn
items.text: Hello, Ana. This is a message about your appointment at the Green Clinic. The time is now four o’clock this afternoon, not three. The address is the same. Please come to reception ten minutes before your appointment. You don’t need to reply if four is OK. If you need another time, please call reception. Thank you.

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: Hi, Ana! The forecast says it will rain on Sunday morning. Let’s use our backup plan. If it rains, we’ll go straight to the museum, and we’ll have lunch inside.

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: We can still take the nine o’clock bus. If that bus is late, let’s wait for the nine thirty one rather than walk in the rain. Does that work for you?

items.speaker: Ruby
items.text: Hi, Ana. I’ve checked what happened at the entrance in our concert story. They couldn’t get in immediately because one person had left their wristband at home. The entrance was still open at eight twenty, so closing time wasn’t the problem.

items.speaker: Ruby
items.text: The help desk could issue a replacement if they showed the digital ticket. They eventually got in, but the opening act had already finished. Could you explain the sequence to someone who thinks they were turned away because they arrived late?

items.speaker: Owen
items.text: Hi, Ana. I’ve had another call about the repair. He said he couldn’t come on Thursday after all and would come on Friday at eleven instead. He still asked us to leave the spare key at reception. He also said the visit might take longer than an hour if the tap needs replacing. Could you pass that on to the building manager and check that the new time has been understood? The earlier Thursday booking should be removed from the diary.

items.speaker: Niamh
items.text: Hi, Ana. Taking the bus is much easier now. I’m used to checking the timetable before I leave, so I haven’t missed the last bus again. The cold is still difficult, especially deciding what to wear when the weather changes during the day.

items.speaker: Niamh
items.text: I’ve joined a weekly group, but I sometimes feel homesick in the evenings. It isn’t all wonderful or all terrible! What helped you get used to a different routine? I’d really like to hear your experience.

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: Hi, Ana. There’s one more detail about that short course. The unexpected benefit wasn’t a job offer. The person met someone who later invited them to help with a community project. They still collaborate now, and that work has made it easier to explain their skills to other people.

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: If they hadn’t gone to Toronto, that particular collaboration might not exist today. But it would be too strong to say they’d have no opportunities at all. Could you explain the present consequence and then describe a plausible alternative, making clear which part is a fact and which part is only a possibility?

items.speaker: Evelyn
items.text: Hi, Ana. Reception checked the booking and agrees that breakfast was already included in the room price. They can return the twenty-dollar breakfast charge if we provide the receipt reference; it may take three business days. The fifty-dollar deposit is different. It will be assessed after the room check at departure, so it hasn’t been approved for return yet. Could you explain which amount we can request now and which condition still applies to the deposit? We don’t need to give any bank details in this practice conversation.

items.speaker: Ruby
items.text: Hi, Ana. I’ve checked the flat. The door is locked, the stove is off, and the iron is unplugged. The window was open, so I’ve closed it as you asked. I haven’t watered the plants yet because you wanted to decide the timing first. Would you like me to water them today or come back on Saturday? I can do either. Please send that one instruction when you have a moment. Everything else on the list has been checked, so there’s no need to ask me to repeat the whole routine.

items.speaker: Owen
items.text: Hi, Ana. The source has clarified the café notice. The dining area is closing for renovation, and delivery will continue, but a reopening date has not been set. The earlier post’s claim of permanent closure is not supported by the official notice. Could you revise the update with that attribution intact?

items.speaker: Owen
items.text: Please don’t replace the false certainty with a confident reopening date. If people need to plan a visit, the useful next step is to check the café’s own updates rather than repeat the same unverified post. We can explain what the notice confirms and what it leaves open without implying that every part of the original rumour has been investigated independently.

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: Hi, Ana. The supplier has confirmed that the lower quote of four thousand eight hundred is available on the thirteenth of December. The budget limit remains five thousand. That resolves the pending supplier date, but it doesn’t automatically confirm the team’s availability or authorise the spending. Could you update both briefings?

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: The funding person now has a costed option to review; the rota organiser can ask who is available for that date. Please preserve the distinction between a supplier confirmation and our own final event confirmation. We don’t need to repeat the colour discussion or every abandoned suggestion. A useful summary gives the decision, its reason and the next action for this particular recipient.

items.speaker: Niamh
items.text: Hi, Ana. I’ve read the event update, but I’m not sure what you need from me. When you say “please acknowledge”, do you only want me to confirm I’ve seen the message, or do you need to know whether I can attend on Monday? I can send either, but they aren’t the same commitment. Could you also give the response deadline as a day and time rather than “tomorrow”? I sometimes read messages after the day they were sent. The new date, same ten o’clock start and room two are clear. It’s the requested action that needs clarification, so there’s no need to rewrite every factual detail or make the wording more elaborate.

items.speaker: Owen
items.text: A quick update about our next study session. We’ll use audio only, so we won’t share screens or code. Choose one feature from your practice project. Explain what it does and who would use it.

items.speaker: Owen
items.text: One more thing: tell me what you tested and what you still want to improve. Send me a short voice note before we meet. If you’re stuck, include the error message and one thing you’ve already tried.

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: For the technical interview, we’ll use a customer portal login. A customer enters an email and password. With a wrong password, the form should stay open and show a clear error. Please explain how you would investigate and test that behavior.

items.speaker: Priya
items.text: You don’t need to prepare slides or write code during the call. Bring one real or practice project and explain your own contribution. We’ll leave time for your questions about the team, and I’ll send feedback by Friday.
